title: DCN V2: Improved Deep & Cross Network and Practical Lessons for Web-scale Learning to Rank Systems
layout_note: Both panels are the proposed model in two arrangements (stacked vs parallel), not proposed-vs-baseline.
grouping: Two variants of the same network side by side: a stacked structure at left (embedding, then cross network, then deep network, one above the other) and a parallel structure at right (cross and deep networks side by side over a shared embedding). Each sub-network is a thin black dotted rectangle with a small grey label inside its corner (Embedding Layer, Cross Network, Deep Netwrok). A small legend box at the top centre lists the circle colours.
shapes_depth: Every layer is a dashed rounded pill holding a row of filled circles, labelled at its right in bold math (x0, x1, x2, x_l1, h1, h2). Circle colours encode role: dense features orange, sparse features light orange, embeddings light grey, cross-layer units yellow, deep-layer units taupe, output dark olive. Cross operations are small circled-x glyphs fed by a thin black skip line from x0 running up the left side; a circled-slash glyph marks the deep-layer step. Inputs enter as orange circles at the bottom with short arrows; vertical dots stand for omitted layers. Flat, no shadows.
proposed_highlight: No single element is singled out; the proposed cross layers are the yellow rows, distinct from the taupe deep layers, and the figure presents both proposed arrangements at equal size.
lesson: Draw each layer's vector as a row of circles in a dashed pill, coloured by role (dense/sparse input, embedding, cross, deep) with one legend, and route the x0 skip line up the side into every ⊗ so the cross structure reads without text.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year (2008.13535); venue WWW from Semantic Scholar (venue_source: semantic-scholar), not stated on the PDF's first page. 'Deep Netwrok' is spelled so in the figure. elements 'other' = neuron circles inside dashed layer pills.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: click-through rate prediction / learning to rank

core.what: two DCN-V2 variants side by side: on the left the cross network stacked under the deep network, on the right the two networks placed in parallel over one shared embedding layer

relations.form: two whole architectures left and right, the stacked variant as one column of dotted frames and the parallel variant as two side-by-side frames joined at a concatenated top layer
bottom to top in each variant: embedding layer, cross layers x_1 ... x_l1, then deep layers h_1 ... h_l2, ending in one output dot
a long line from x_0 rises along the left edge and enters a circled-x node below every cross layer, drawing that each cross layer multiplies by the original input
in the parallel variant one embedding layer frame at the bottom feeds both the cross-network frame and the deep-network frame

channels.colour: keyed in a legend: dark orange = dense feature, light orange = sparse feature, light grey = embedding, yellow = cross layer, grey = deep layer, brown = output
channels.shape: circles = units/neurons; circled-x = the crossing product; circled slash = activation
channels.line: solid arrows only, all data flow
channels.frame: dotted frame = one sub-network (embedding layer, cross network, deep network); dashed rounded frame = one layer of units

quality.strengths: The two structural alternatives are drawn with the same glyph vocabulary so the only difference is placement (stacked vs parallel); the x_0 feed into every cross layer is a single straight vertical bus with short horizontals, making explicit crossing visible; colour is one meaning (unit type) and keyed.
quality.weaknesses: No (a)/(b) titles on the two variants; 'Deep Netwrok' misspelt twice; in the stacked variant the x_0 bus runs from the bottom-left embedding all the way up with long horizontal returns; panels differ in width so the comparison is not perfectly aligned.

insights.structure: Two complete variants side by side: on the left a stacked design (Embedding Layer, Cross Network, Deep Network piled bottom to top in dotted frames), on the right a parallel design where the Cross Network and Deep Network sit next to each other above a shared Embedding Layer.
insights.data: Every layer is a dashed rounded row of coloured circles, with colour as type (dark orange dense, light orange sparse feature, grey embedding, yellow cross layer, dark grey deep layer, brown output) and math labels x0, x1, x2, x_l1, h1, h_l2 at each row's right.
insights.emphasis: Cross layers are the only yellow units and the circled-x operator between rows plus the long line from x0 feeding every cross layer make the explicit feature-crossing visible.
insights.flow: Bottom to top; in the right panel x0 fans out into both towers and their final rows are concatenated into one wide top row before the single output dot.
insights.avoid: The labels 'Deep Netwrok' are misspelt twice and the two variants carry no (a)/(b) titles, so the panels must be told apart from the caption.

arrangement.units: Two variant panels; within each, dotted rectangles enclose Embedding Layer, Cross Network and Deep Network, each holding dashed rounded rows of circles.
arrangement.inputs_as: small orange circles (sparse features) with arrows into the embedding row x0
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; a single brown output circle at the top
arrangement.shared: the embedding layer x0 feeds both cross and deep towers in the right panel
